## Discovery & Translational Science

- **Proteogenomic atlas maps type 2 diabetes trajectories and GLP-1 response persistence**
  - Researchers constructed the Metabolic Atlas of the Proteome in Diabetes (MAP-D) using Olink profiles of 2,923 circulating proteins across ~42,000 UK Biobank participants combined with semaglutide clinical trial proteomics.
  - Mendelian randomization delineated distinct causal architectures: adiposity predominantly alters the circulating proteome, whereas glycemia is driven downstream of systemic protein changes.
  - Trial integration identified key proteins normalized by GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy alongside a subset of dysregulated proteins that persistently resist normalization despite semaglutide treatment.

- **Spatial proteomics identifies immunosuppressive "Myelonets" in ovarian cancer**
  - Single-cell spatial proteomics and transcriptomics across 50 high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC) tumors identified six distinct spatial microenvironment patterns, dominated by macrophage-rich communities termed Myelonets.
  - Following chemotherapy, persistent Myelonets demonstrated coordinated lipid metabolism and immunosuppressive transcriptional profiles (*SPP1*, *C1Q*, *VEGF*, *MMPs*, *CCL18*) driven by fibroblast interaction, correlating with poor response to immune checkpoint blockade.

- **Urinary collagen type I peptides identified as shared pan-fibrotic biomarkers**
  - Capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry (CE-MS) peptidomic profiling across cohorts with chronic kidney disease (n = 263), heart failure (n = 187), and liver disease (n = 127) identified shared naturally occurring urinary collagen type I (COL1) degradation products.
  - The identified COL1 degradation signature reflects ongoing extracellular matrix remodeling and offers a common non-invasive marker for progressive tissue fibrosis across multiple organ systems.

- **Distinct LRRK2 haplotype linked to slower motor decline in Parkinson’s disease**
  - A 12-year longitudinal analysis of 603 participants in the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) evaluated motor symptom trajectories across specific *LRRK2* variants.
  - Carriers of the *LRRK2* R1441G+M1646T co-occurring haplotype exhibited significantly slower motor symptom progression (MDS-UPDRS III) compared to patients carrying isolated *LRRK2* mutations or sporadic Parkinson's disease.

- **[Isthmin-2 identified as early biomarker for preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04573-6)** — *Nature Medicine*
  - Serum proteomics profiling identified Isthmin-2 (ISM2) as a functional mediator of extravillous trophoblast invasion.
  - Reduced serum ISM2 levels during early pregnancy correlated with an increased risk of developing preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction.

- **[Systemic fluconazole remodels gut microbiome and lowers disease activity in IBD](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04616-y)** — *Nature Medicine*
  - A prospective observational study in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients with oral thrush evaluated systemic fluconazole versus topical nystatin therapy.
  - Orogastrointestinal fluconazole, but not localized nystatin, significantly altered intestinal mycobiome/microbiome structure and reduced clinical disease activity at 8 weeks.

- **[Serum big tau distinguishes peripheral neuropathies from CNS disorders](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.27.26361202)** — *medRxiv*
  - Assayed serum big tau (a peripheral nervous system-predominant isoform), brain-derived tau (BD-tau), and neurofilament light chain (NfL) via Quanterix Simoa across patients with GBS, MFS, CMT, CIDP, MS, AD, and healthy controls.
  - Big tau was elevated in Guillain-Barré syndrome compared to other neuropathies, central nervous system disorders, and healthy controls.

- **[Tumor-adjacent B-cell infiltration predicts prostate cancer recurrence](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.29.26361718)** — *medRxiv*
  - Performed transcriptomic profiling on paired tumor and adjacent non-cancerous tissue across discovery (n = 123) and validation (n = 120) cohorts undergoing radical prostatectomy.
  - B-cell infiltration in tumor-adjacent benign tissue stratified the risk of postoperative biochemical recurrence or PSA persistence.

- **[Advanced brain age in major depression develops post-onset rather than as baseline vulnerability](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.29.26361710)** — *medRxiv*
  - Evaluated longitudinal structural MRI data in 3,220 individuals, including 78 healthy controls who transitioned to a first depressive episode during the study.
  - MRI-derived brain age was elevated by 1.4–2.5 years in established major depressive disorder, but pre-onset scans showed normal baseline brain age, disproving advanced brain aging as a pre-existing structural vulnerability.

- **[TAVI alters gut metabolome and short-chain fatty acid dynamics](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.30.26361742)** — *medRxiv*
  - Profiled 16S rRNA, circulating short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and cytokines in 40 patients undergoing elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) pre- and 3 months post-procedure.
  - TAVI reduced gut microbial richness without altering overall community composition; post-procedural SCFA changes were linked to the IL-18 inflammatory response.

- **[Visual awareness neurosignatures evaluated across Alzheimer's disease severity](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.27.26356661)** — *medRxiv*
  - Measured visual awareness negativity (VAN) and late positive (LP) responses using no-report visual masking paradigms with EEG and fMRI in mild-to-severe Alzheimer's disease.
  - Identified persistent functional activation patterns in visual and fronto-parietal networks, offering objective markers of perceptual awareness independent of verbal reporting capacity.

- **[Mechanistic model projects shift to kidney-centric risk during extended spaceflight](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.27.26360881)** — *medRxiv*
  - Calibrated a 12-state Ca-bone-urine differential equation model on International Space Station (ISS) data and simulated Mars mission conditions (730 days).
  - Extended partial-gravity exposure increased lumbar bone mineral density loss (-12.15% Mars vs -4.83% ISS) while renal stone rates dropped (13.1 vs 16.1 per 1,000 person-years), shifting primary physiological risk from bone resorption to urinary chemistry alterations.

- **[Multicenter validation of AI-derived epicardial adipose tissue reference percentiles](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.28.26360111)** — *medRxiv*
  - Created sex- and age-specific nomograms for CT-measured epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume and density in 42,842 patients undergoing myocardial perfusion imaging.
  - Percentile thresholds for body surface area-indexed EAT predicted adverse cardiovascular outcomes over a median 3.6-year follow-up.

- **[Alinity high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay matches ARCHITECT for 30-day risk stratification](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.29.26361405)** — *medRxiv*
  - Secondary analysis of the POC-ET study evaluated Abbott's Alinity hs-cTnI assay against the ARCHITECT assay using sex-specific 99th percentile upper reference limits (34 ng/L for men, 16 ng/L for women).
  - Confirmed strong agreement between assays for single-sample rule-out pathways predicting 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death.

- **[Evidence audit re-evaluates late-stage cancer incidence as trial surrogate endpoint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.29.26361733)** — *medRxiv*
  - Re-assessed 1,209 candidate records to audit 26 eligible reports representing 18 cancer screening trials.
  - Evaluated the trial-level correlation between late-stage incidence reduction and cancer-specific mortality to test endpoint robustness following data harmonization.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Novartis and BMS pause early-stage autoimmune CAR-T trials over safety concerns](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novartis-bristol-myers-autoimmune-cell-therapy-trial-halt/829218/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Novartis temporarily halted Phase 1/2 clinical studies of its rap-cel T-cell therapy across lupus, myasthenia gravis, and multiple sclerosis following three reports of immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome (IEC-HS), a severe hyperinflammatory reaction.
  - Bristol Myers Squibb voluntarily paused enrollment in its clinical-stage autoimmune cell therapy program to evaluate emergent safety signals across its trial portfolio.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Combination belimumab and rituximab evaluated in primary membranous nephropathy**
  - Full results from Part A of the Phase 2 REBOOT trial (NCT03949855) evaluated weekly subcutaneous belimumab (200 mg) for 52 weeks combined with intravenous rituximab (1,000 mg at weeks 4 and 6) in 17 patients with primary membranous nephropathy and severe proteinuria (≥4 g/day).
  - At week 104, 59% (10/17) of intention-to-treat participants achieved complete or partial proteinuria remission; heavy baseline proteinuria (>9 g/day) did not significantly impair belimumab drug exposure.

- **Adjunctive psychobiotic PS128 demonstrates clinical benefit in major depressive disorder**
  - A 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated adjunctive *Lactiplantibacillus plantarum* PS128 (6 × 10¹⁰ CFU/day) in patients with MDD receiving stable escitalopram therapy.
  - PS128 significantly improved clinical response and remission rates over placebo on HAMD-17 and MADRS scales, corresponding to dynamic enrichment of short-chain fatty acid-producing gut microbiota (*Faecalibacterium*, *Coprococcus*) and suppression of *Klebsiella* expansion.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Biotech]** **[Cytokinetics presents detailed Phase 3 Myqorzo data at ESC 2026](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/esc-congress-2026-results-eplontersen-alnylam-cytokinetics/829139/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Detailed Phase 3 data for Myqorzo (aficamten) in non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) were published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* and presented at the European Society of Cardiology Congress.
  - The trial establishes Myqorzo as the first selective cardiac myosin inhibitor to demonstrate significant clinical efficacy in both obstructive and non-obstructive HCM populations.

- **[Big Pharma]** **J&J presents Phase 3 Vivacity-MG3 ocular subgroup outcomes for nipocalimab**
  - Subgroup data from the pivotal Phase 3 Vivacity-MG3 study evaluated the FcRn blocker nipocalimab in generalized myasthenia gravis patients presenting with moderate-to-severe ocular symptoms.
  - Nipocalimab administration produced meaningful reductions in ocular disease burden and muscle weakness compared to placebo over the primary treatment interval.

- **Phase 3 trial validates ferric citrate for hyperphosphatemia in Chinese hemodialysis cohort**
  - A multicenter, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial evaluated the safety and phosphate-binding efficacy of oral ferric citrate tablets in Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia undergoing maintenance hemodialysis.
  - Ferric citrate successfully met its primary serum phosphate lowering endpoint with a safety profile consistent with prior global Phase 3 regulatory trials.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Atezolizumab misses primary EFS endpoint in Phase 3 NSABP B-59/GeparDouze trial in early TNBC](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04565-6)** — *Nature Medicine*
  - Adding atezolizumab (Tecentriq) to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) did not significantly improve event-free survival (EFS).
  - Translational analysis indicated efficacy was restricted to specific tumor microenvironments, with potential EFS benefit observed in basal-like immune-activated tumors.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Biotech]** **[FDA approves Takeda and Protagonist's Mimrylo (rusfertide) for polycythemia vera](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/fda-approve-mimrylo-takeda-protagonist-polycythemia-vera/829153/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - The FDA approved Mimrylo (rusfertide), a first-in-class peptide hepcidin mimetic co-developed by Takeda Pharmaceutical and Protagonist Therapeutics, to control erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera.
  - The regulatory approval granted a broad label that does not require prior treatment failure with second-line cytoreductive therapies (such as ruxolitinib); the commercial list price was set at $4,200 per vial.

- **[Biotech]** **[FDA approves Besremi for essential thrombocythemia](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/fda-approves-treatment-essential-thrombocythemia)** — *FDA*
  - Approved ropeginterferon alfa-2b-njft (Besremi) for adult patients with essential thrombocythemia based on efficacy data from the SURPASS ET study.
  - Dosing starts at 250 mcg subcutaneously, increasing to 350 mcg at 2 weeks, and maintaining at 500 mcg every 2 weeks.

- **[FDA collaborates on non-animal endotoxin testing methods via ICMRA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/international-collaboration-advance-new-testing-methods-reduce-reliance-horseshoe-crab-blood)** — *FDA*
  - Evaluated alternative non-animal endotoxin testing methods for biologics through the ICMRA Collaborative Assessment Pilot to decrease reliance on horseshoe crab blood.
  - Implemented a synchronized 120-day review timeline across international regulators to streamline global regulatory assessments.

- **[FDA releases M11 harmonized clinical protocol guidance and ARC rare disease resources](http://www.fda.gov/about-fda/accelerating-rare-disease-cures-arc-program/rare-disease-news-events)** — *FDA*
  - Released final M11 guidance, templates, and technical specifications for standardized, digital clinical trial protocols.
  - Published six new case studies and educational materials under the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research's (CDER) Accelerating Rare disease Cures (ARC) LEADER 3D initiative.

- **[FDA issues CGMP warning letter to Seema International](http://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/seema-international-716072-11132025)** — *FDA*
  - Issued Warning Letter 320-26-19 citing significant CGMP deviations in active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing at Seema International's New Delhi facility following a May 2025 inspection.

- **[FDA safety updates highlight Tazverik market withdrawal and product recalls](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/drug-alerts-and-statements)** — *FDA*
  - Highlighted increased risks of secondary blood cancers associated with Tazverik (tazemetostat), leading the sponsor to initiate a voluntary market withdrawal; CDER also proposed withdrawing approval for Tavneos (avacopan).
  - Announced a nationwide voluntary recall of Lipofit Extreme Fat Burner 2.0 due to contamination with undeclared fluoxetine and 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP).

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Eli Lilly acquires Merida Biosciences in $2.9B deal](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/lilly-merida-acquire-deal-immune-drugs-graves-disease/829152/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Eli Lilly expanded its immunology platform by acquiring privately held Merida Biosciences for up to $2.9 billion in upfront cash and prospective developmental milestones.
  - The deal secures Merida’s platform designed to selectively target and clear pathogenic autoantibodies implicated in autoimmune disorders such as Graves' disease.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Amgen patent acquisition strategy faces antitrust legal scrutiny](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/08/31/pending-drug-patent-applications-amgen-carefirst/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT News*
  - Antitrust litigation involving Amgen and health insurer CareFirst is drawing industry attention over whether corporate acquisition of pending, unissued patent applications can be legally categorized as an anti-competitive tactic to extend product monopolies.

## Public Health & Policy

- **[White House announces nine additional drug pricing agreements](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/31/trump-most-favored-nation-drug-pricing-new-round-price-cuts-announced/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT News*
  - The Trump administration announced agreements with nine additional pharmaceutical companies to lower domestic prescription drug prices under its most-favored-nation pricing initiatives.

- **[NIH proposal to cap grant counts meets researcher resistance](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/01/nih-grant-cap-proposal-researcher-feedback/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT News*
  - An NIH policy proposal seeking to establish a hard cap on the total number of active research project grants an individual investigator can hold has received mixed feedback from academic institutions and principal investigators.

- **[Incorporating avian dynamics improves West Nile virus forecasting accuracy](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.27.26361564)** — *medRxiv*
  - Evaluated 15 years of surveillance data in Maricopa County, Arizona, using four mechanistic disease models.
  - Models integrating both weather forcing and avian reservoir dynamics significantly improved 1- and 2-week-ahead forecast accuracy for human and vector infection rates over baseline models.

- **[Longitudinal genomic surveillance maps antimicrobial resistance trends in Canada](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.27.26361471)** — *medRxiv*
  - Analyzed prescribing patterns, whole-genome sequences, and susceptibility data from 23,063 bacteraemia isolates across five bacterial pathogens from 2006 to 2022.
  - Mapped strain-specific sequence type trajectories across hospital-onset and community-onset cases to track AMR response to prescription changes.

- **[Pre-vaccination immunity variance skews observational vaccine effectiveness estimates](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.29.26361716)** — *medRxiv*
  - Modeled continuous risk distributions of pre-vaccination infection risk across vaccinated and unvaccinated cohorts over time.
  - Demonstrated that heterogeneity in baseline population immunity can cause significant divergence between observational vaccine effectiveness (VE) estimates and true biological protection, generating artifactual negative VE.

- **[Age-stratified seasonality observed in alcohol-associated emergency department visits](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.27.26361527)** — *medRxiv*
  - Analyzed 45,876 alcohol-associated emergency department visits from NEISS (2019–2025; weighted estimate 2,092,319) across five adult age brackets.
  - Cosinor analysis demonstrated significant age-dependent variations in the timing and predictability of seasonal peak injury risk.

- **[Validation of Patient Safety Screener-3 for depression screening in physicians](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.30.26361711)** — *medRxiv*
  - Cross-sectional nationwide survey of 1,844 resident physicians in Japan evaluated the PSS-3 suicide risk tool against the PHQ-9.
  - PSS-3 item 1 (depressive mood) demonstrated 79.3% sensitivity for PHQ-9 confirmed depression (≥ 10), with 2.5% of residents meeting full PSS-3 high-risk criteria.

**Worth watching:** Detailed biomarker subgroup results from Roche's Phase 3 NSABP B-59/GeparDouze trial, as the efficacy observed in basal-like immune-activated TNBC may inform future biomarker-driven patient selection for neoadjuvant checkpoint inhibition.
